title: Say a failed claim in her window: the runner's problem and run phases have no reader
body:
## Summary
The task runner records why a claim failed (`useTaskRunner.problem`) and each task's phase (binding, working, waiting on a card), but nothing draws either, so a claim that throws leaves the strip saying "in line" with no reason.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/task-runner.ts:153-159` declares `useTaskRunner` with `runs` and `problem`; `:233-235` sets `problem: "A delegated task could not be started: ..."` when `POST /tasks/claim` throws. `git grep -n useTaskRunner apps/desktop/src` finds only task-runner.ts and its test: neither her strip (`apps/desktop/src/companion/tasks.tsx:82-98`, which reads `useTasks` only) nor Main's card shows them. ADR 0141 makes her window the executor, so a claim that keeps failing (a daemon 500, a rotated token) is invisible: the row stays `queued`, the strip says "#1 in line", nothing says why. Fixed: the strip says the runner's problem (one quiet line, as the mirror's problem is said) while a task is queued, and may show `waiting` for a task resting on a card.

## Flow
- Her window: a task is delegated; `claimTask` rejects (500)
- task-runner sets useTaskRunner.problem
- companion/tasks.tsx reads only useTasks: the row says "#1 in line" forever, no sentence

## Expected impact
The person sees why a delegated task never starts. Could break: the strip's quiet-by-design rule - say the problem only while a task is queued.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a claim failure is said where the task is shown
Before: 0 surfaces read useTaskRunner (grep: task-runner.ts and its test only)
After: not built - the surface is companion/tasks.tsx, outside this round's paths
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep; the decider is a strip test (claimTask rejects -> sentence shown)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
$ git grep -n useTaskRunner apps/desktop/src
apps/desktop/src/stores/task-runner.ts:159  export const useTaskRunner = create<TaskRunnerState>(...)
apps/desktop/src/stores/task-runner.test.ts:31,260,332,366,378,433,465,578,584,600
apps/desktop/src/stores/task-runner.ts:235  useTaskRunner.setState({ problem: `A delegated task could not be started: ...` })
instrument: companion/tasks.test.tsx: claimTask rejects -> the strip shows the runner's sentence while a task is queued; red on today's tree

title: Stop counting failed and killed tasks as "finished" in the task summary
body:
## Summary
The strip's and Main's summary counts every ended task as "finished", so three failures read "3 finished".

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/tasks.ts` `summaryOf`: `ended = shown.length - running - queued` and says `${ended} finished`; ended holds done, failed, killed and interrupted (`shownTasks` keeps all four for RECENT_MS). "2 running · 3 finished" reads as success. Options: "3 ended", or "1 done · 2 failed". A word choice for the owner, and the one-line summary has little room.

## Flow
- Three delegated tasks fail within ten minutes
- The strip's summary reads "3 finished"
- The rows below it say failed

## Expected impact
The summary stops reading as good news when it is not. Could break: tests asserting "finished"; Main's first-frame bytes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the summary does not dress failures as finished
Before: summaryOf counts failed/killed/interrupted as "finished" (read)
After: depends on the word chosen
Method: simulation - the summary for three failed rows; the rung above needs the word first
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Say the dock's due line without two different "more"s
body:
## Summary
The dock's due line can read "Chore a is due (and 2 more since) · 1 more due": the first "more" counts missed occurrences of this chore, the second other chores waiting.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/console/due-notice.tsx` builds `since = " (and ${notice.missed} more since)"` and `queued = " · ${more} more due"`. The review says the first one plainly (`apps/desktop/src/scenes/chores/due-model.ts` dueLine: "2 more came and went since"). A wording such as "Chore a is due (missed 2 times) · 1 other chore due" separates them; the house voice decides.

## Flow
- A chore missed twice is due while another chore waits
- The line reads "... is due (and 2 more since) · 1 more due"

## Expected impact
The line is read at a glance in the dock. Could break: due-notice tests asserting the line's text.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one line, two counts that cannot be confused
Before: both counts are "more" (read)
After: depends on the words chosen
Method: simulation - the line for missed=2, more=1
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Read the task runner's tab deadlines from its injectable clock, not Date.now
body:
## Summary
`bind()` measures TAB_OPEN_MS and TOOLS_WAIT_MS against `Date.now()` while it sleeps through the injectable `deps.wait`, so no test can drive the "tab never appeared" failure without 10 s of real time.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/task-runner.ts:445` `const until = Date.now() + TAB_OPEN_MS` and `:451` `const ready = Date.now() + TOOLS_WAIT_MS`, in loops that sleep with `deps.wait(100)`; `RunnerDeps.now` (`:113`) already exists for stamps. A test with an instant `wait` spins until real time passes 10 s, so the `no_page: the tab opened for ... never appeared` branch is unpinned. Fixed: read a deps clock (ms) in both loops and add the test.

## Flow
- Test: deps.open answers a tab id that never appears in deps.tabs()
- wait resolves at once
- The loop runs until real Date.now passes 10 s

## Expected impact
The tab-open timeout and the tools wait become testable in milliseconds. Could break: nothing in the running app (LIVE keeps Date.now).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the two deadline branches get a fast test
Before: 0 tests reach "never appeared" (grep of the test file)
After: not built this round
Method: simulation - read the loops and the deps seam
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: task-runner.test.ts: a fake ms clock advanced by wait(); the never-appearing tab fails with no_page in <100 ms real time
